title: Self-Boundary Dissolution in Meditation: A Phenomenological Investigation

claims.statement: Across n=46 practitioners' phenomenological reports of volitional self-boundary (SB) dissolution, six experiential categories (sense of agency, self-location, first-person perspective, attentional disposition, body sensations, affective valence) were derived by qualitative coding, then a PCA on five of them (excluding valence, which was uncorrelated with the rest) found ONE component explaining 58% of variance, with high loadings on all five (Agency 0.83, Location 0.85, FPP 0.84, Attention 0.78, Body 0.80). The resulting unweighted sum score correlated r=0.91 with an independent holistic dissolution rating.
claims.scope: N=46 proficient meditators (115-24,837 lifetime practice hours), SB- (dissolve boundaries) condition only -- the SB+ (maintain boundaries) condition had too little variance for the same analysis to be meaningful (noted explicitly by the authors as a limitation, though similar association PATTERNS held, Supplementary Figure S3).

our_assessment.why: The unitary-dimension finding is real within this instrument and this population (advanced practitioners doing a specifically designed SB-dissolution task), and the authors themselves flag the natural over-generalization risk: 'different clusterings...would have been plausible' (Section 4.6), and a PCA cannot distinguish 'one true underlying process' from 'these five measured categories happen to be highly correlated in this specific task design'. Bearing on CAT: it is independent, primary-source support (not recalled, not assumed) for treating self/boundary dissolution as approximately one CAT dimension (D-self) rather than needing several sub-axes -- but the caveat about task-design-induced correlation applies equally to CAT's own eventual dimension count and should be stated with the same hedge, not borrowed as a clean precedent.

claims.statement: Sense of Agency (deliberate control vs. passive letting-go) and Attentional Disposition (focused vs. wide/formless) are the most central, causally load-bearing dimensions in a partial-correlation network of the SB dissolution categories -- Agency has the highest node-strength centrality, Attention second. The specific meditation techniques of 'relaxation, release, passivity' and, to a lesser degree, 'turning attention outwards' most strongly predict degree of dissolution in a linear model (p<=0.001 and p<=0.05 respectively against other techniques); both act by reducing active attentional/agentic engagement rather than by any content-reappraisal move.
claims.scope: N=46, SB- condition, network analysis (Figure 2A/B) and linear model on DD_C by technique (Figure 2C).

our_assessment.why: Read directly from the paper's own reported statistics, not recall. Directly useful for CAT's D-self rubric: the strongest, most expertise-correlated markers of self-boundary dissolution are AGENCY and ATTENTION language, not 'self' or 'boundary' vocabulary as such -- concrete instructional anchors for D-self should include letting-go/release/relaxation-of-control language and wide/formless-attention language, mirroring what this study finds actually drives the phenomenon, at least in this specific SB-dissolution task design.

claims.statement: The authors explicitly connect intrusive thoughts disrupting deep SB dissolution to Lutz et al.'s dereification construct (citing lutz2015 directly, Section 4.3): a wandering thought 'which comes with form' breaks the formless quality of deep dissolution, and they gloss this as 'related to a high level of dereification'. In their framework, dereification functions as a FACILITATING/PROTECTIVE mechanism for sustaining self-boundary dissolution (keeping attention free of thought-content that would re-introduce form/boundary), not as a definition or a component of self-boundary dissolution itself, which is instead driven primarily by agentic/attentional disengagement (see c2).
claims.scope: Section 4.3, a single explicit citation and gloss, not a tested claim of this paper's own -- the authors did not measure dereification directly, they interpret one qualitative observation through Lutz's construct.

our_assessment.why: This is the primary-source bridge between the two lineages I have been trying to reconcile since cat_lutz_crosswalk.md's blocking question (2026-08-13): the embodied-self empirical group itself treats dereification as instrumental to sustaining boundary dissolution, not as constitutive of it or identical to it. This is a THIRD framing, distinct from both my two prior candidates (Lutz's 'species-of' content reduction, and my own 'functionally separable structural dimension' reading): dereification-of-intrusive-thought as a maintenance condition for an independently-driven (agency/attention) process. Worth folding into CAT's D11/D-self discriminant-validity discussion as a third hypothesis to test against real transcripts, not just the two already on record.

claims.statement: Self-boundaries (SB) and body-boundaries dissociate, sometimes in a counter-intuitive direction: in the SB+ (maintain boundaries) condition, participants performed narrow body-scan meditation which sharpened body-boundary definition, but this often coincided with a MORE observer-like, LESS embodied sense of self (body experienced as an object -- Korper -- perceived BY an observing self, rather than directly lived through -- Leib). Maintaining tight bodily focus did not straightforwardly maintain a strong embodied self; it could instead produce distance from it.
claims.scope: Section 4.2, qualitative synthesis across the SB+ condition interviews.

our_assessment.why: A genuine, non-obvious empirical dissociation directly relevant to CAT's D2 (Somatic Engagement) and D-self: a CAT transcript with high D2 (tight body focus, body-scan instructions) should NOT be assumed to predict low D-self engagement (strong embodied self) by default -- this paper's own data shows the opposite can occur (body focus producing observer-distance). Worth a specific discriminant-validity check once transcripts are scored: does D2 correlate positively, negatively, or not at all with D-self, and does it depend on whether the body-focus instruction is scanning/locating (Korper-inducing) vs. dwelling/inhabiting (Leib-sustaining)?

relations.why: c3 (this record) cites the same dereification definition from lutz2015 and extends it with an explicit functional role (facilitating/protective for boundary dissolution) that lutz2015 does not itself specify for the self-boundary case -- lutz2015 only discusses self-disidentification as a species of dereification (its own #c3), not dereification as a maintenance condition for an independently-driven boundary-dissolution process.

Both studies treat self/boundary structure as empirically tractable via a small number of derived dimensions from first-person report, and both find it clusters into fewer dimensions than the raw category count suggests (gamma2021: an 11-18-factor questionnaire nonetheless yields one especially load-bearing self/observer factor; nave2021: six categories collapse to one PCA component at 58% variance). Neither paper tests whether their own reduction is a property of the phenomenon or of their measurement design -- both should be read with that shared, unstated assumption flagged.

open_questions: Does CAT's own instruction corpus contain enough boundary/self-inquiry instructions with enough variance to test whether D-self genuinely factors as ONE dimension (as this paper and, more weakly, gamma2021-mpe92m both suggest) rather than needing an agency sub-axis and an attention sub-axis kept separate -- given that THIS paper's own D-self-analog (Agency+Location+FPP+Attention+Body) is already close to what CAT would call D1 (Attentional Constraint) + D-self + D2 (Somatic Engagement) combined, the 'unitary dimension' finding might be an artifact of not having separated attentional-constraint language from self-structure language in their coding scheme to begin with.

The technique-level finding (relaxation/release most predictive, turning-attention-outward second) gives CAT concrete instruction-level anchors for D-self -- draft rubric anchors from this before the next CAT rubric-writing pass, don't let it sit as a read paper only.
